title: Kenyan Roasted Groundnuts
author: Mama Wanjiru
desc: Kenyan Roasted Groundnuts — raw peanuts dry-roasted in a pan until perfectly toasted, fragrant, and crunchy, then salted and sold in paper cones at every roadside. The simplest, most universally loved Kenyan street snack.
longDesc: Karanga — roasted groundnuts — are everywhere in Kenya. Sold by vendors at bus stops, street corners, markets, and stadia, they are the nation's most portable snack. The skill is in the roasting — too short and they are raw and starchy; too long and they are bitter. Perfectly roasted groundnuts have a deep nuttiness, a satisfying crunch, and a natural sweetness that makes it almost impossible to stop at one handful.
ingredients: 500g raw groundnuts (peanuts) — in their shells or shelled
1 tbsp fine sand or coarse salt — for oven roasting method (traditional)

substitutions.alternative: Chilli salt for a spicy version

steps: Pan method: place raw groundnuts in a large, dry, heavy pan over medium heat.
Stir continuously and constantly for 15—20 minutes.
The groundnuts are done when the skins begin to split and peel, the colour has darkened to a deep golden, and they smell deeply nutty.
Remove from heat immediately — they continue to cook from residual heat.
Spread on a flat surface to cool.
Rub the groundnuts between your palms to remove the papery skins if desired.
Season with salt while still warm. Serve in paper cones.
chefTips: Constant stirring is non-negotiable — groundnuts burn quickly once hot. Never leave the pan.
Remove from heat when they smell deeply nutty — they continue to cook for 2—3 minutes from residual heat.
The traditional Kenyan sand-roasting method (roasting in hot sand) gives incomparably even results — approximate this by using a very heavy pan that retains heat evenly.
commonMistakes: Leaving the pan unattended — groundnuts burn in seconds once hot.
Too high heat — outside burns before inside is cooked.
Not removing promptly — continue to cook from residual heat and can over-roast.

faqs.q: Can I roast groundnuts in the oven?
faqs.a: Yes — spread on a baking tray and roast at 180°C for 15—18 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes. Watch carefully in the last 5 minutes.

faqs.q: How do I know they are done?
faqs.a: The skins split and begin to peel, the colour darkens to a deep golden-brown, and the aroma changes from raw to deeply nutty and toasted. Bite one open — it should be evenly golden throughout, not white in the centre.

cookingScience: Roasting groundnuts causes the Maillard reaction between the amino acids and sugars in the nut, producing hundreds of new flavour compounds — the characteristic deep, complex nuttiness of roasted peanuts that raw nuts do not possess. The heat also reduces moisture content, creating the characteristic crunchy texture.
sustainabilityTips: Groundnuts are a nitrogen-fixing legume — they enrich the soil they grow in.
Buy from local Kenyan groundnut farmers at markets.
storage: Store in an airtight container for up to 2 weeks at room temperature.
reheating: Not required — serve at room temperature.
healthBenefits: Rich in plant protein — 14g per serving.
High in healthy monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fats.
Good source of magnesium, niacin, and folate.
Contains resveratrol — an antioxidant with cardiovascular benefits.
culturalNote: Roasted groundnuts are the most universally eaten street snack in Kenya — sold in paper cones at every bus stop, market, and public gathering. The groundnut vendor, with their heavy roasting pan and the smell of toasting peanuts, is as much a part of the Kenyan street landscape as the matatu or the ugali pot.
